processing: As with other Fujian white teas, the leaf is not fired or rolled: a long wither followed by drying does nearly all the work, with only slight oxidation.
harvest_season: Little is documented for Songxi specifically. As is usual in northern Fujian white tea country, spring is the main and most prized picking.
appearance_dry: Described as tightly knotted strips of green colour, which is unusual for the class. Lots differ, so go by the leaf in front of you.
appearance_liquor: Pale yellow-green to light apricot and clear, as is usual for lightly withered Fujian white tea.
appearance_wet: Soft, intact buds and leaves in pale green, as is typical of the class.
taste_profile: Described as having a clear aroma and a mellow taste, and as standing up well to repeated steeping. Beyond that, expect the class profile of northern Fujian white tea: a light body and a gentle sweet return.

brewing.notes: General guidance for Fujian white tea. Go by the leaf: bud-heavy lots take cooler water and leafier ones can go hotter.

vintage_note: No selling pattern particular to Songxi is well documented. As usual for Fujian white tea, expect the current year's spring harvest sold fresh, with some lots kept or pressed and sold by year as aged tea. Ask for the harvest year and the cultivar.
description:
Songxi is a county in Nanping, in northern Fujian, and it sits on the usual short list of the province's white tea areas alongside Fuding, Zhenghe and Jianyang. It is much less known than those neighbours, and most drinkers will never see its name on a packet.

The making follows the Fujian pattern: no firing and no rolling, only a long wither and then drying. One short description gives it tightly knotted green strips, a clear aroma, a mellow taste and good staying power over repeated steeps, and credits the county's warm climate, rainfall and fertile soil.

Detailed tasting descriptions of Songxi as its own tea are scarce, so treat the rest as the class norm: a light sweet cup and a soft finish. Short steeps with water a little off the boil suit it.

If you find one, ask which cultivar it uses and which year it was picked. The county name alone says little.
history: Songxi is documented as a white tea producing county in northern Fujian. Little is documented about when white tea making began there or who developed it.
